text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-01: I re-derived every quantitative claim independently. `grep -n 'safety:' app.js` returns exactly 25 hits at the 25 lines cited (147,157,167,177,187,199,209,219,229,239,251,261,271,281,291,303,313,323,333,343,355,365,375,385,395). The sole read is app.js:640 (`${drug.safety}` inside the openDrugModal template literal, app.js:606-643); nothing parses, derives or validates it. `git ls-files` confirms the platform is README.md + app.js + index.html + styles.css only; no model, no manifest, no output JSON, no HTTP call, no descriptor code. The distributional forensics are exact, not approximate: 24 rows carry the byte-identical string 'hERG IC50 > 50 μM' and 1 (app.js:147) the same value with '(0% Cardiotoxicity)' appended; Seizure Index appears in 21/25 rows with exactly {0.00: 9, 0.01: 8, 0.02: 4}; and a Python extraction of the third pipe-delimited slot returns exactly 22 distinct labels. Every count the reviewer asserts reproduces. BLOCKER is the right call: README.md:98 ('All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening') has no referent whatsoever. Correction: Two factual imprecisions, neither altering the finding. (1) The file inventory is wrong: the repo also tracks skills-lock.json and a ~200-file .agents/skills/ library that includes chembl-database and alphafold-database skills with real analyze_plddt.py / analyze_pae.py scripts. None is wired to the platform, so the conclusion stands, but an absence-claim in a fabrication review must be exact. (2) The claimed 'zero hits' grep is overstated — 'clearance' matches at app.js:64, 112, 333, 359 and README.md:89. The defensible statement is 'no pharmacokinetic clearance anywhere; the only clearance hits are efficacy language about lysosomal and glutamate clearance.'

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-02: README.md:99 reads verbatim 'IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)' and app.js:147 '(0% Cardiotoxicity)'; both verified in situ. All three margin computations reproduce exactly in Python: 50/30 = 1.67 μM, 50/37 = 1.35 μM, 50/50 = 1.00 μM, and at the peptide MW I computed independently (4943.0 Da, average residue masses + water) those are 8.24, 6.68 and 4.94 mg/L. The Leishman citation is real and says precisely what is claimed — PMID 32768644, J Pharmacol Toxicol Methods 105:106900, n=367, CredibleMeds means 4.8/28/71/339, and the abstract states verbatim that ROC-optimal thresholds were '37- and 50-fold, respectively.' Lehmann PMID 29380488 likewise gives 0.312 (95% CI 0.205-0.476, p<0.0001) and a negligible-risk ratio of 80. The three-part critique is correct: a 0% claim is unfalsifiable, risk is a ratio whose denominator is absent, and a byte-identical single-significant-figure value across 25 chemically distinct entities is not a measurement or a prediction. Correction: (1) Same absence-grep overstatement as AIML-01: 'clearance' does appear, as efficacy language. Rephrase to 'no pharmacokinetic or exposure parameter of any kind.' (2) The reviewer enumerates the zero-risk claims but misses a fourth: app.js:375 asserts 'BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%', which belongs in the same deletion list as '0% Risk', '0% Cardiotoxicity' and 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%'.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-03: The premise-falsification is airtight. I read every cited linker: app.js:183 (GGGGS), 235 (GGGGS), 277 (GGGSGGS), 287 (two GGGGS), 339 (GGGGS), 391 (GGGGS), 125 (GGGGSGGGGSGGGGS), 126 (GGSGGSGGSGGSGGS), 129 (GGGSGGS). Every peptide linker in the platform is Gly-Ser. Kyte-Doolittle G = -0.4 and S = -0.8 are correct. My own physicochemistry on the 36-mer reproduces the reviewer's to three decimals: GRAVY -1.09 (exact), Eisenberg hydrophobic moment 0.615 (exact), MW 4943.0, 13 Lys+Arg vs 4 Asp+Glu (exact). Both supporting papers are real and say what is claimed: Pardo-Lopez PMID 11864985 identifies Trp-585, Gly-590, Ile-593 (S5-P) and Pro-632 (P-S6) as the outer-vestibule determinants of ErgTx binding; Zavarzina PMID 38563123 shows BeKm-1 Arg20 forming a salt bridge plus hydrogen bonds with the vestibule and R20K dramatically reducing activity. The mechanistic sentence at README.md:99 is false against the repo's own sequence data and names a site the modality cannot reach. Correction: (1) 'There are no hydrophobic linkers in this platform' is too broad — app.js:182 declares a '1,2,3-Triazole Linker', app.js:194 a 'Trans-Cinnamoyl Linker', app.js:298 an 'Azide Linker'. None is a peptide linker, so README.md:99's specific phrase 'hydrophobic peptide linkers' remains false, but narrow the sentence to peptide linkers or the author refutes it in one line. (2) My net-charge calculation gives +8.79 at pH 7.4 rather than +8.98; the ~0.19 offset is a pKa-set difference (N-terminus) and is immaterial, but quote a pKa set. (3) The Tyr652/Phe656 attribution is given only as 'Ala-scanning of S6 and the pore helix; see e.g. Mitcheson-type SAR literature' — that is a gesture, not a citation, and I could not verify it as written. In a report whose thesis is unsourced numbers, replace it with a specific reference or delete the parenthetical.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-04: Verified line by line: README.md:100 states 'Seizure Index = 0.01 - 0.02 / 1.0 (Negligible)' with 'capped Emax (135%)'; app.js:219 carries '(Capped Emax 135%)'; 21 of 25 rows carry a Seizure Index taking only {0.00, 0.01, 0.02}. The target classes are as cited: GluN2A NTD modulation (app.js:215-220), α7 nAChR ECD PAM (app.js:195-200), M1 mAChR PAM with explicit M-current suppression and increased burst firing (app.js:257-262), AChE gorge block raising synaptic ACh +350% (app.js:246-252). Cholinergic overdrive and M-current suppression are textbook proconvulsant mechanisms; the reported values invert the true risk direction. Cohen PMID 39661496 is real and the key numbers are exact: the integrated 11-target panel gives sensitivity 68%, specificity 56%, accuracy 65%, with Cav2.1 the highest-importance single target. Bradley PMID 29432603 is real: MEA on cryopreserved rat cortical neurons, 12 spike-train parameters, 20 chemicals, 16/17 seizurogenic/neurotoxic compounds detected. No standardized 0-1 seizure index exists; the metric is invented. Correction: (1) The Cohen evaluation set is misstated. The abstract says the 11-target panel was assessed against 34 preclinical compounds and 10 approved drugs; an *additional* 35 approved drugs were run in the Cav2.1 assay alone. 'against 34 preclinical compounds and 45 approved drugs' overstates the panel's evidence base. Also note the 68/56/65 figures are specifically for predicting convulsion in nonclinical species from the preclinical compound set. (2) Bradley used rat cortical neurons only; the reviewer's 'rodent cortical or hiPSC-derived' generalizes beyond the cited paper. (3) A stronger adjacent point is left on the table: app.js:251 pairs the most seizurogenic candidate in the portfolio (ACh +350%) with 'Peripheral Side Effects: None' — see missed_by_reviewer.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-05: The core claim survives fully. README.md:102 reads verbatim 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days. Biased agonist signaling redirects receptors to recycling endosomes'; app.js:147 '< 3.5%', app.js:157 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%', app.js:187 '< 3.8%', app.js:199 'Receptor Desensitization: Low', app.js:261 'Desensitization: Safe'. A 30-day receptor-downregulation percentage is a chronic in vivo pharmacodynamic endpoint requiring repeat dosing plus Bmax/surface-biotinylation/immunoblot quantification and a vehicle arm; the repo contains no dose, route, species or PK model. No in-silico method outputs it. The bias rationale is equally unsupported — no operational-model fit, no ΔΔlog(τ/K_A), no β-arrestin readout, no Rab11-vs-Rab7 trafficking data. Correction: One sub-claim is factually wrong and must be struck. The reviewer writes that HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (app.js:157) has 'no receptor for it to downregulate, so the endpoint is not merely unmeasured, it is inapplicable.' That inverts the pharmacology. Chronic cholinesterase inhibition is the classical cause of muscarinic receptor downregulation and pharmacodynamic tolerance: Costa, Schwab & Murphy (Biochem Pharmacol 1982;31:3407-3413, PMID 7150362) showed 2 weeks of anticholinesterase dosing reduced forebrain muscarinic Bmax by 40% with cross-tolerance to oxotremorine. Tolerance is therefore *more* pertinent to the AChE-inhibitor candidates, not inapplicable — which makes 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%' at app.js:157 the single most inverted string in the file rather than a category error. Separately, the biased-signalling ground truth is supported only by bare 'PMC6620903' and 'PMC3952036' with no title, author, year or journal; I did not retrieve either and they cannot be checked as given. Replace with full citations or drop them.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-06: Verified. README.md:101 and app.js:167, 271, 303, 323, 343 read as quoted. Grep over README.md, app.js and index.html for MHC|epitope|NetMHC|EpiMatrix|ADA|anti-drug returns zero — no immunogenicity analysis of any kind exists. My own frame enumeration reproduces the reviewer's counts exactly: the 36-mer yields 22 15-mer frames (22 with F/W/Y/L/I/V/M in positions 1-6) and the 100-mer at app.js:125 yields 86 frames (53 with such a residue). The innate/adaptive conflation at README.md:101 is a real category error — TLR4/MD2 antagonism cannot reduce MHC-II presentation of the construct's own sequence. Both methodology citations are real (NetMHCIIpan-4.3, PMID 38000035; ISPRI/EpiMatrix/JanusMatrix, PMID 38536724), and the AN1792 6% meningoencephalitis figure is confirmed independently in PMID 25860060 and PMID 21592055. Correction: (1) The P1-anchor screen flags 22 of 22 frames — a filter with a 100% hit rate conveys no information and should be presented as an illustration of unscored scale, not as evidence of epitope content. The reviewer's own 'candidate' hedge is right; the surrounding framing ('are therefore candidate P1-anchored MHC-II binders') overstates it. (2) The AN1792 analogy needs a caveat and is then stronger than stated. AN1792's meningoencephalitis is attributed to Th1 responses against T-cell epitopes in the mid/C-terminal region of Aβ delivered with QS-21 adjuvant — which is exactly why the second-generation vaccines named in PMID 25860060 (CAD106, ACC-001, AFFITOPE) restricted the antigen to the Aβ1-6 B-cell epitope. The repo's payload is Aβ16-35, squarely inside the region those programs deliberately excluded. An unadjuvanted conjugate is not the same exposure as an adjuvanted vaccine, so the 6% rate is not transferable — but the epitope-selection argument is more precise and more damaging than the raw incidence figure.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-07: The physicochemistry is fully reproducible and I confirm it to three decimals on independent code using the Eisenberg consensus scale at 100°/residue: KWWKFLRRFWRR μH 0.989, MW 1865.3; FLRRFWRR μH 1.068, MW 1236.5; the 36-mer μH 0.615, GRAVY -1.09, MW 4943.0; melittin 0.353; LL-37 0.559. Every value matches the reviewer's. Grep confirms zero occurrences of hemoly/cytotox/aggregat/protease/proteoly outside the one efficacy hit at app.js:334. The substantive point is correct and important: the panel reports a small-molecule CNS liability set for peptides while omitting every peptide-specific liability. The reviewer's calibrated refusal to over-claim toxicity — citing Deslouches PMID 27046192, where WK12/WR12 showed negligible haemolysis and cytotoxicity up to 10× MIC — is exactly right and is the most scientifically disciplined passage in the review. Correction: (1) 'Trp/Arg-rich cationic 8-12-mers of exactly this composition are a well-characterized engineered-AMP series' is wrong on 'exactly'. The Deslouches eCAP series is composed *exclusively* of Trp plus Arg or Trp plus Lys; KWWKFLRRFWRR also contains Phe and Leu. Analogous chemotype, not identical composition. (2) 'peptides of 4-5 kDa with strongly negative GRAVY do not cross the blood-brain barrier' is stated too absolutely — brain-penetrant peptide shuttles and Arg-rich CPPs achieve measurable CNS uptake. The defensible form is that unmodified polycationic 4-5 kDa peptides have negligible passive BBB permeability and require an explicit delivery strategy, which the repo does not have. (3) Severity: lower to MAJOR. This is a missing-capability finding that asserts no false fact of its own and is largely subsumed by AIML-01; labelling five separate items CRITICAL beneath a BLOCKER parent is severity inflation that dilutes AIML-02/03/04/08, which each assert something affirmatively false.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-08: The alignment is exact and I reproduced it against Aβ42 (DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA): KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM = Aβ16-35, KLVFFAED = Aβ16-23, KLVFFA = Aβ16-21, GAIIGLM = Aβ29-35. app.js:275 does label it 'AChE-Aβ Fibril Disruptor' and app.js:281 does read 'Fibril Blockade: 100%'. My physicochemistry on the app.js:277 construct reproduces the reviewer's GRAVY of +0.26 exactly (net charge +0.84 vs their +1.03, a pKa-set offset) — a near-neutral hydrophobic peptide, uniquely so in this portfolio. Balbach PMID 11076514 is real and states verbatim that Aβ16-22 is among the shortest fibril-forming fragments of full-length β-amyloid reported to date, with an antiparallel β-sheet organization and β-strand conformation extending from Leu17 through Ala21. 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' is a fabricated completeness claim on top of a directionally inverted design. Correction: The conclusion is right but the reasoning is one-sided and refutable as written. KLVFF is the canonical *recognition* motif for Aβ-targeting inhibitor design: Tjernberg et al. (J Biol Chem 1996;271:8545-8548, PMID 8621479) showed that peptides incorporating KLVFF (Aβ16-20) bind full-length Aβ and prevent its assembly into fibrils, and that work founded the whole KLVFF-based inhibitor class. So 'a wild-type copy of the CHC is a seed, not a breaker' is too strong as a general proposition and hands the author a one-move rebuttal. The precise version: (a) KLVFF as a recognition element is legitimate and precedented; (b) the hazard is the *extension* to Aβ16-35, which appends the second hydrophobic segment GAIIGLM (Aβ29-35) and yields an unmodified 20-mer spanning both aggregation-driving regions at near-neutral charge and positive GRAVY; (c) Balbach establishes that even the shorter Aβ16-22 self-assembles into ordered amyloid; (d) no register-disrupting modification (Pro, N-methyl, D-residue) is present anywhere in the construct. Also, the supporting 'PMID 21309606, PMID 35134456' are given bare with no titles and I did not verify them — supply full citations or remove.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-09: Verified by extraction rather than inspection. Parsing the third pipe-delimited slot across all 25 records returns exactly 22 distinct labels, confirming the count; the second slot returns only 3 (Seizure Index, Cytokine Storm Risk, BBB Disruption Risk), so no two candidates share a full endpoint set and cross-candidate safety ranking is genuinely impossible. Every efficacy-flavoured field cited is real and sits under the heading 'ADMET Safety Profile & Side Effects' at app.js:639: Lysosomal Clearance +420% (app.js:333), Inflammatory Cytokine Suppression 98% (app.js:313), Vasodilation Rate +45% (app.js:355), Tau Hyperphosphorylation Suppressed (app.js:229), Fibril Blockade 100% (app.js:281). No interval, coverage level, probability, model identity, version, training set, AD verdict, timestamp or git SHA appears anywhere. The conformal-prediction, Chemprop and ADMET-AI citations (PMIDs 33075380, 38147829, 38913862) all resolve to real papers with the stated titles and venues. Correction: (1) The enumerated label list contains 23 items, one of which ('Cytokine Storm Risk') belongs to the second slot, not the third. The count of 22 is right; the list is not. Trim it. (2) A missed opportunity rather than an error: this is the one finding where the reviewer looks directly at the `affinity:` literals (app.js:146-394) and concludes only that they lack uncertainty. They are also internally impossible — ΔG and Kd cannot both be true for any of the 25 records, and the same sequence is assigned three different pLDDT values. That is a stronger, fully objective falsification and belongs here. See missed_by_reviewer items 1-3.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-10: Verified verbatim. app.js:381 reads `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` and app.js:385 gives it a full ADMET profile ('hERG IC50 > 50 μM | Seizure Index: 0.00 | Cerebral Edema: Prevented'). The character B — the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx, rejected by AlphaFold Server for protein chains — appears in app.js:173, app.js:371 and app.js:130. All three of these plus the prose string flow unchecked through app.js:648-652 into initModal3DCanvas (app.js:708-729), renderModalPlddtChart (app.js:787-795) and renderModalPaeHeatmap (app.js:844-865). The reviewer is right that this is the cleanest single proof for AIML-01: no cached upstream computation can have existed if a prose string and an invalid residue code both render a safety profile and a confidence curve. Correction: (1) The copy-button count is wrong. copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) reads `currentActiveModalSequence`, which is set only from FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA at app.js:600. Exactly three copyable entries are invalid (app.js:173, 371, 381); the AF3 rank-6 fasta at app.js:130 is rendered at index.html:291 with no copy control. Three, not 'at least four'. (2) Severity: raise to MAJOR. The reviewer under-weights its own best evidence. This is not merely a missing guard — renderModalPlddtChart will emit and plot a per-'residue' AlphaFold3 confidence profile labelled L1 i2 n3 k4 e5 r6 for the letters of the English word 'Linker', under a heading that reads 'AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model & PAE Heatmap Graphs' (index.html:371). That is affirmatively misleading rendered output, not an engineering hygiene gap, and it sits in the same class as the fabricated safety strings.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE SINGLE LARGEST MISS — ΔG and Kd are thermodynamically impossible for all 25 candidates, and the reviewer read these exact strings (AIML-09 cites app.js:146-394) without checking them. ΔG = RT·ln(Kd); at 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol. Every pair is irreconcilable: X1 reports ΔG -18.4 kcal/mol with Kd 0.32 nM, but -18.4 implies Kd = 3.3e-5 nM (off by 9,828×); B5 reports -19.5 with 0.08 nM against an implied 5.1e-6 nM (15,730×). Across all 25 the discrepancy is 3.85-5.73 kcal/mol, i.e. 665-15,730× in Kd. Yet Pearson r(ΔG, ln Kd) = 0.997, so the two columns were generated from one another by a wrong formula; regressing gives an implied RT of 1.056 kcal/mol, i.e. a binding temperature of 531 K (258 °C). This is a two-line arithmetic falsification requiring no domain judgement and no literature, it is more objective than the distributional argument in AIML-01, and it independently destroys the 'affinity' half of the platform. It belongs in the report as a BLOCKER alongside AIML-01.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: pLDDT is a deterministic function of the input sequence, and the platform assigns the same sequence three different values. KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG appears verbatim at app.js:153 (pLDDT 94.8, ΔG -16.2, Kd 2.1 nM), app.js:247 (94.3, -17.5, 0.65 nM) and app.js:131 as AF3 rank 7 (92.8, -12.6). Four further collisions: app.js:173 vs 371; app.js:195 vs 319; app.js:205 vs 361; and app.js:163 vs the AF3 rank-3 fasta at app.js:127 (97.0 vs 96.1). One molecule cannot have three AlphaFold3 confidences or three binding free energies. The reviewer cited app.js:153/247/131 as the same peptide (AIML-07) and did not notice the metrics conflict — a cleaner proof of fabrication than any statistical argument in the review.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The duplicate sequences directly falsify a specific safety string the reviewer never tested. The identical 41-mer at app.js:195 and app.js:319 is claimed to bind α7 nAChR ECD (Tyr188/Trp149/Tyr195) and TLR4/MD-2 (Arg264/Lys341/Glu439); the identical 37-mer at app.js:205 and app.js:361 is claimed to bind TrkB D5 and the EAAT2 transporter; the identical 31-mer at app.js:173 and app.js:371 to bind Frizzled-8 CRD and the ZO-1/occludin complex. app.js:209 — on one of those very rows — asserts 'Off-target Binding: None'. Demonstrated intra-repo promiscuity across four unrelated receptor families refutes the platform's only selectivity claim from its own data, which is exactly the off-target polypharmacology competence AIML-07 invokes but does not exercise.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: SEVEN OF EIGHT SMILES STRINGS ARE UNUSABLE, WHICH MAKES THE REVIEW'S PRIMARY REMEDIATION IMPOSSIBLE AS WRITTEN. I parsed all eight in RDKit 2026.03.5. Four do not parse at all: Huperzine A (app.js:10), Curcumin (app.js:50 — the terminal 'OCH3' is an illegal token outside brackets and ring-closure 3 is unmatched), Onjisaponin V (app.js:60) and Salvianolic Acid B (app.js:70), the latter two being bare molecular formulas typed into a field the UI renders as 'SMILES Formulation' (app.js:477). Two parse but encode the wrong molecule: Ginsenoside Rg1 gives C38H64O14 not C42H72O14, and Ginkgolide B gives C18H22O8 not C20H24O10. Baicalein parses to the correct formula but the wrong regioisomer — InChIKey SXZJEWVPXPKGJG-UHFFFAOYSA-N, which is 6,7,8-trihydroxyflavone, not baicalein/5,6,7-trihydroxyflavone (FXNFHKRTJBSTCS-UHFFFAOYSA-N). Only Asiatic Acid is constitutionally correct, and it carries zero stereochemistry despite ~9 stereocentres. The reviewer instead praised this module as 'largely correct, checkable literature pharmacology... the strongest part of the repo,' and then proposed in AIML-01 step (2) to 'run ADMET-AI or Chemprop v2 over the warhead SMILES' — which cannot execute, because half the inputs are not molecules. Structure repair and RDKit round-trip validation must be step zero of any remediation plan.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The rendered 'pLDDT' is provably incapable of expressing the confidence bands the UI advertises, and the code contains dead guards that prove it. app.js:791 computes score = 93 + sin(i·0.4)·4 + (charCode % 5)·0.5, whose analytic range is 89.0 to 99.0. The guards at app.js:792-793 (`if (score > 100)` and `if (score < 70)`) are therefore unreachable dead code, and the legend at index.html:390-391 declaring 'Low (50-70)' and 'Very Low (<50)' bands can never be exercised. Worse, the 3D 'pLDDT Color Spectrum' at index.html:377 is coloured at app.js:747-749 by amino-acid identity (G/S green, P/D amber) — a lookup on the letter, not on any confidence value. Since AlphaFold reliably assigns low pLDDT to poly-GS linkers and disordered cationic peptides, the one region guaranteed to score low is the one this code paints green. This is a concrete, self-contained falsification of README.md:108-109 and Section 4.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: A section titled 'In Silico ADMET' contains no A, D, M or E. Across README.md:96-102 and all 25 rows the only endpoints are hERG, a fabricated seizure index, and one rotating third slot. Entirely absent: absorption/permeability (Caco-2, PAMPA), plasma protein binding, BBB permeability, CYP inhibition and induction, DDI risk, metabolic stability, clearance, half-life, DILI/hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, Ames/genotoxicity, phototoxicity, and the ICH S7A secondary-pharmacology panel. A senior reviewer must publish the missing-endpoint inventory, because 'the T is fabricated' understates the problem — the ADME is not fabricated, it was never contemplated, and the section name is itself a misrepresentation.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: 'Peripheral Side Effects: None' (app.js:251) is the most directly falsifiable safety string in the file and goes unmentioned. It is attached to BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, whose stated mechanism at app.js:252 is elevating synaptic acetylcholine by +350%. The approved cholinesterase inhibitors — donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine — carry labelled nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, anorexia, bradycardia, syncope and AV block. This also exposes a conceptual gap in AIML-02: for a cholinomimetic, cardiac risk is not principally a hERG question at all — vagotonic bradyarrhythmia is mediated through muscarinic tone and would be invisible to any hERG assay, so even a genuine 'hERG IC50 > 50 μM' would not clear these candidates cardiologically.

tags: AI/ML for ADMET and toxicity property prediction — cheminformatics, computational safety pharmacology, model calibration and applicability domain
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The natural-product warheads are dominated by frequent-hitter chemotypes, and the review praises them instead. Curcumin (app.js:48-56, and the payload of app.js:298 and app.js:338) is formally classified as both a PAINS and an IMPS compound: Nelson, Dahlin, Bisson, Graham, Pauli & Walters, 'The Essential Medicinal Chemistry of Curcumin', J Med Chem 2017;60(5):1620-1637, PMID 28074653, concludes it is unstable, reactive, non-bioavailable and 'a highly improbable lead', with no successful double-blind placebo-controlled trial among >120 attempts. Baicalein and salvianolic acid B are polyphenol/catechol redox-cyclers and colloidal aggregators in the same interference class. Flagging assay-interference and bioavailability liabilities in the input chemotypes is core ADMET competence; the review's 'what is done well' section instead endorses this module, which is the one place the report overstates the repo's quality.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI)' is an invented metric that outranks everything the review did flag, and the source code admits it. CEI is hardcoded to three significant figures for all ten AF3 candidates (app.js:125-134), is the ranking column of the leaderboard (index.html:306), and is plotted at app.js:1053-1076 on a shared axis against |ΔG| in kcal/mol — a dimensionally meaningless comparison. The function that draws it sits under the author's own comment at app.js:1048: '--- Chart.js Benchmark Simulation ---'. A source comment conceding simulation, directly above the platform's headline benchmark, is the strongest single piece of intent evidence in the repository and the review never quotes it. In the same class: index.html:42 renders a badge reading 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' that is a static hyperlink with no connection of any kind, and README.md:24 and :111 claim 'direct live integration' — so the review's praise of the AlphaFold integration as 'the one place the platform behaves honestly' needs qualifying to the copy-FASTA control alone.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: Two smaller in-domain defects. (a) Chemical formula error: app.js:266 gives 'Ginsenoside Rg3 Dammarane Core (C36H62O8)', which matches neither ginsenoside Rg3 (C42H72O13) nor its protopanaxadiol aglycone (C30H52O3); the other formulas I checked (Rg1 C42H72O14, Rb1 C54H92O23, curcumin C21H20O6, baicalein C15H10O5, ginkgolide B C20H24O10, bilobalide C15H18O8, asiatic acid C30H48O5, huperzine A C15H18N2O, presenegenin C30H46O6) are correct, so this one is an outlier worth a line. (b) No reference or control compounds: a 25-candidate safety panel that never runs donepezil, memantine, galantamine or a known hERG blocker and seizurogen through the identical pipeline has no scale, no calibration and no way to demonstrate that its numbers discriminate anything. Positive and negative controls should be a required element of the AIML-09 schema, not an optional extra.
